clue.text: Good landlord, reverse of fool, has branches in Oz (8, two words)

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a tree rather than a noun

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
a host keeps an inn

indicators.note: asks for the following word's synonym written back to front

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person

explanation.surface: A pub landlord who is the opposite of a fool has opened several branches in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' looks like a chain of pubs, but the definition is a tree with branches, and Oz is Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The ghost gum is a white-barked Australian eucalyptus, so it is a tree with branches growing in Oz.

clue.text: Gloucester's opener on nought, first dismissed — certainly won't appeal!

indicators.note: dismissed means sent off, so the first letter is removed
an opener comes first, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: initial letter
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing

explanation.surface: A Gloucestershire opening batsman is out for nothing, and no bowler need bother appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. The cricket picture is the decoy: the definition is about something unappealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Guck is a slang word for slimy, messy gunk, which certainly holds no attraction.

clue.text: Mihrab mostly reconstructed in Muslim holy place

indicators.note: something reconstructed is rebuilt in a different form, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a mihrab is the prayer niche in a mosque

explanation.surface: A mosque niche partly rebuilt inside a sacred site.
explanation.definitionFit: Harim is a variant of harem, literally a sacred or forbidden place in Arabic usage.

clue.text: Informers? See nameless one sing to slop deviously (12, two words)

indicators.note: something devious takes a winding route, so the letters wander out of order
nameless means lacking a name, so the abbreviation for name is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch an anonymous informant spill everything to a dirty mess.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name comes out of ONE. 'Sing' looks like part of the picture, since informers sing, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool pigeon is slang for a police informer, originally a decoy bird used to lure others.

clue.text: One gets ecstatic about number lifting these weights

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read bottom to top
about means around, so one word is wrapped round the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: sent is slang for transported with delight
the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A weightlifter gets a thrill out of raising these heavy loads.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole picture of a delighted lifter is the decoy; 'One gets' only leads into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonne is a metric unit of mass equal to a thousand kilograms.

clue.text: I'll be on the way up in great territory — I know what I want

indicators.note: placed in means set inside the following abbreviation

parts.note: GT is the abbreviation for great, as in Gt Britain

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I
an abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: An ambitious person heading upwards in a vast land declares a clear sense of purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person, as the answer would about itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter is an ambitious, determined person who knows exactly what they are after.

clue.text: Tom's sound, if not strong, in heaving mass of forwards

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the following one

parts.note: a maul is a rugby scrum-like tussle among forwards

indicators.note: not strong drops the musical symbol for forte from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written, losing its F

explanation.surface: A rugby forward named Tom makes a noise from within a struggling pack.
explanation.walkthrough: A tom is a male cat; F is forte, loud or strong, in music. Tom looks like a player's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Miaul is an old word for a cat's mew, so it is the noise a tomcat makes.

clue.text: Is gran wavering in purpose? Far from it

indicators.note: placed in means set inside the following synonym

parts.note: intent means purpose

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so the letters shift about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether granny is losing her resolve, and answering no.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition answers the question: 'far from' wavering.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent means unwilling to compromise, the opposite of wavering.

clue.text: The old scare, endless increase in years

indicators.note: placed in means set inside the following synonym

parts.note: an age is a long span of years

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: An old fright about prices rising without limit over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an archaic word, not an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrise is an obsolete verb meaning to terrify or to shudder with fear.

clue.text: Limits of exuberance in brief affair evaporating

indicators.note: placed in means set inside the following synonym

parts.note: a fling is a short romance

indicators.note: limits are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: its outermost letters

explanation.surface: High spirits vanishing during a short romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeing can mean vanishing or passing swiftly away, as fleeting time or dissolving mist does.

clue.text: HE, tiddley, tottering

indicators.note: tottering means swaying unsteadily, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk man staggering home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'HE' looks like a pronoun, but it is the abbreviation for high explosive; tiddley is British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyddite is a picric-acid explosive once used in shells, so it is a high explosive.

clue.text: Get to work, entering one by one in subservient fashion?

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so these letters sit within the next phrase's synonym

parts.note: the first letter of the word meaning one at a time
taken as written
OP is short for opus, a work
the rest of the word meaning individually, one after another

explanation.surface: An instruction to start working by going in one person at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' just tells you to fetch the pieces; the definition's question mark admits that stooping is a posture standing in for servility.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop is to bow or condescend, so behaving stoopingly means acting with servile, bowed humility.

clue.text: Crosby's first on list for Jock … of those that do?

definitions.text: Crosby's first on list for Jock … of those that do?

indicators.note: placed on means one piece is followed directly by the next in the down-the-page sense of reading
the first of a name means only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the singer's name
roon is Scots for a selvage or strip of cloth, which is also called a list

explanation.surface: Bing Crosby tops a Scotsman's list of those who sing in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby was the archetypal crooner, so the whole clue also hints at what he and his like do. 'Jock' is a nickname for a Scot, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooning is soft, sentimental singing, the style that made Crosby famous, so it is what those crooners do.

clue.text: Junction? Went fast round it in spite

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to hare is to run very quickly
a T-junction, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Someone sped round a road junction out of malice.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the junction is a T-junction, giving just the letter. The 'it' after 'round' stands for that junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and hatred are both strong feelings of ill will towards someone, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Benzene derivative, or nearest the same

parts.note: one's nearest are one's close relatives
as in 'all one', meaning identical

explanation.surface: A chemistry question about a compound derived from benzene, or its closest relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearest and dearest' means family, hence the kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinone is a variant spelling of quinone, an organic compound obtained by oxidising benzene derivatives.

clue.text: Deeply engrossed, was picking brambles, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the spelling comes from a different word pronounced the same

parts.note: to berry is to go gathering berries such as blackberries

explanation.surface: Someone absorbed in blackberrying.
explanation.walkthrough: Brambles are blackberries, and to berry is a verb for picking them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be buried in something, like a book, idiomatically means to be wholly absorbed in it.

clue.text: Use malt for distilling in magic potions?

definitions.note: Chambers gives amulet an old sense of a remedy thought to work by occult power

indicators.note: distilling breaks a substance down and recombines it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to turn malt into whisky that acts like a magic brew.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: amulets are usually charms worn, but the dictionary records them as occult medicines too.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm believed to protect by supernatural means, and in an older sense a magical remedy.

clue.text: Sabbath churchgoers? They may be seen playing on the lawn

definitions.text: They may be seen playing on the lawn

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for Sabbath
those who pray at a service

explanation.surface: Churchgoers on a Sunday, afterwards seen at play on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' suggests games, but sprayers play water as fountains play.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden sprinklers spray water over grass, and water jets are said to play, so these devices play on lawns.

clue.text: Sound of a bump making wife jump

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
to hop is to jump

explanation.surface: A sudden thud makes someone's wife leap in alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Whop is an imitative word for the dull noise of a heavy blow or fall.

clue.text: Clinch? Women, fidgety, avoiding final coupling

indicators.note: a coupling is a pair, so the last two letters are left off

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
restless means fidgety

explanation.surface: A wedding dance where a fidgety woman avoids the final embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: A clinch is a grappling hold, as in boxing, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinch is a grip in which fighters grapple, which is what wrestlers do.

clue.text: Boys turned on by girls, say, impassioned over love

definitions.text: Boys turned on by girls, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so one piece comes first

parts.note: het, as in het up, means heated or excited
Eros is the god of love

explanation.surface: Young men aroused by young women, fervent about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Heteros is informal for heterosexuals, people attracted to the opposite sex, of whom such boys are an example.

clue.text: Imprisoned on being captured in early western

indicators.note: whatever is captured is held inside, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: pent means shut up or confined
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone locked up after being caught in an old cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early western' looks like a vintage film, but it means 'western' in an early, now obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponent is an obsolete word meaning western, from the Latin for the setting sun.

clue.text: Apply fresh acid to eastern river flowing west

indicators.note: in an across clue, moving west means right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
the river that flows through Rome

explanation.surface: Pouring acid again into a river in the east that runs westward.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are turned round together. Etchers bite a plate with acid, so rebiting means a second acid bath.
explanation.definitionFit: In etching, acid bites the metal plate, so to rebite is to give it a further acid treatment.

clue.text: Ingredient of meal often, mostly dry, fed to hobo

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them, so these letters go within

parts.note: a bum is a tramp

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: arid means dry

explanation.surface: A tramp is given a parched portion as part of his supper.
explanation.walkthrough: A barium meal is a liquid swallowed before an X-ray, not a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A barium meal is a suspension of barium sulphate drunk to show the gut on X-rays.

clue.text: Name given to poles supporting wires is to be changed

definitions.text: Name given to poles supporting wires

indicators.note: something changed is altered in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An announcement that the name for telegraph poles is due for renewal.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses 'is to be' together; the indicator overlaps the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stobie pole, named after its inventor, is a steel-and-concrete pole carrying power lines in South Australia.

clue.text: Second one of seven — or any one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
one of the seven ages of man in Shakespeare's 'As You Like It'

explanation.surface: Picking the second from a group of seven, or simply any of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of seven' also hints at the Seven Sages of ancient Greece; the definition widens it to any wise person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is any wise person; the Seven Sages were a famous group of them, but the title fits any one.

clue.text: Son I had, dead captivated by stunner?

indicators.note: captivated by means held by, so these letters go inside the next

parts.note: a knockout punch stuns
contraction of I had
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A boy I fathered fell for a beauty and was dead smitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' looks like a beauty but is a punch that stuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiddo is a familiar form of address for a youngster, such as a son.

clue.text: Flightless birds speed round palm tree

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: rate means speed or pace
the ita is a South American palm, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Ostriches racing round a palm tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratitae is the zoological group of running birds with flat breastbones, such as ostriches and emus, which cannot fly.

clue.text: Once behind in space race, having lost expert airman?

parts.note: an area is a space

indicators.note: having lost means without, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
an ace is a top fighter pilot

explanation.surface: Formerly lagging in the space race after losing a top pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic word; the space race picture is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Arear is an obsolete form of arrear, meaning behind or backward.

clue.text: Rarely dry during late tropical misty rain

parts.note: sere is a literary, seldom-used word for dry or withered
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: Weather report: seldom dry in the tropics, with misty rain coming late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' is not a time word here; it marks the following synonym as a rare usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Serein is the fine rain that falls from a clear sky after sunset, especially in the tropics.

clue.text: Gouty, poorly, accepting recipe for healthy food?

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so a letter is put inside
something poorly is out of sorts, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A gout sufferer, feeling ill, takes a prescription for something wholesome to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for the Latin recipe, 'take', heading a prescription. The question mark admits yogurt's health claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is fermented milk, widely promoted as a nourishing, gut-friendly thing to eat.

clue.text: Riddle: what shows sides but no centre?

indicators.note: having no centre means the middle letter is missing

parts.note: sides in sport are teams

explanation.surface: A puzzle: what has edges but no middle?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle, but it is a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A tems is a sieve, and a riddle is a coarse sieve for soil or grain.

clue.text: Radio set working — as this valve appears?

definitions.text: Radio set working — as this valve appears?

indicators.note: working means operating, so the letters are set in motion into a new order
the dash is read as a minus sign, taking away the little word after it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: When an old wireless is running, this kind of valve shows up inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: early radio sets ran on valves of exactly this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A triode is a thermionic valve with three electrodes, the workhorse of early radio receivers.

clue.text: Bard's beginning to pen Lear (first half) in place where it's calm for him

definitions.text: to pen Lear (first half) in place where it's calm for him

parts.note: the clue's opening words must supply these two letters, though how is not clear: B starts the word Bard, and nothing plainly gives the next letter
the lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: Shakespeare starts writing King Lear in a peaceful spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Belee is a Shakespearean verb, from Iago's 'be-lee'd and calm'd' in Othello, hence 'Bard's'. It is BE plus LEE, but the published clue does not show clearly where BE comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: To belee is to put on the sheltered side, out of the wind, so the whole clue describes doing that to Lear.

clue.text: Dose of corporal punishment in Fettes or Oundle administered by clique

definitions.text: Dose of corporal punishment in Fettes

indicators.note: administered means dealt out, so the letters are dealt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is a closed group of insiders

explanation.surface: A caning at one of two British private schools, dished out by a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: Fettes is a school in Edinburgh and Oundle one in Northamptonshire; 'in Fettes' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Loundering is a Scots word for a beating, so in a Scottish school it is a thrashing.

clue.text: Big fish: I'll make way for group among willows

indicators.note: making way means stepping aside so another takes the place of one letter

parts.note: osiers are willows used for basketry
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A large fish announces it will leave room for a group among the willows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the fish speaking, but it is the letter that gives way.
explanation.definitionFit: The osseter is a large Caspian sturgeon, prized for its caviar, so a big fish indeed.
